# Feed

## Summary
A chronological record of what happened to something — entries with an
actor, a time, a body and a kind. Shared-realm component at
`components/feed.gts`.

## API
- `@entries` — `FeedEntry[]`: `{ id?, actor?, initials?, avatarUrl?, meta?, body?, at?, kind?, hue? }`. Deliberately flat strings rather than card references: a feed is read far more often than it is edited and is frequently rendered where links cannot resolve
- `kind` — `outward` (visible to the other party) / `inward` (our side) / `private` (internal only) / `system` (rendered as a rule across the thread, not a bubble)
- `@newestFirst` — defaults to oldest-first, which is how a thread reads
- `@emptyMessage`, `@onSelect`; `:entry` block replaces body rendering while keeping the chrome

The one rule that matters: a private entry must be impossible to mistake for
a public one — it renders full-width on a coloured ground with an explicit
"Internal — not sent to the customer" tagline.

## Usage
```gts
import { Feed, type FeedEntry } from '../components/feed';

<Feed @entries={{this.entries}} @newestFirst={{true}} />
```

## Example
In use by ServiceDesk's ticket workspace (`components/ticket-workspace.gts`),
which renders each ticket's message thread through it — the linked Ticket is
the live example.

## Non-goals
The feed renders history; it does not collect it. Composers, reply boxes and
the rules for who may post are the consumer's. It also does not paginate —
a consumer with thousands of entries slices before passing.
